title: SPAR: Scalable LLM-Based PDDL Domain Generation for Aerial Robotics
abstract: We investigate the problem of automatic domain generation for the Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) using Large Language Models (LLMs), with a particular focus on unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) tasks. Although PDDL is a widely adopted standard in robotic planning, manually designing domains for diverse applications such as surveillance, delivery, and inspection is labor-intensive and error-prone, which hinders adoption and real-world deployment. To address these challenges, we propose Spar, a framework that leverages the generative capabilities of LLMs to automatically produce valid, diverse, and semantically accurate PDDL domains from natural language input. To this end, we first introduce a systematically formulated and validated UAV planning dataset, consisting of ground-truth PDDL domains and associated problems, each paired with detailed domain and action descriptions. Building on this dataset, we design a prompting framework that generates high-quality PDDL domains from language input. The generated domains are evaluated through syntax validation, executability, feasibility, and interpretability. Overall, this work demonstrates that LLMs can substantially accelerate the creation of complex planning domains, providing a reproducible dataset and evaluation pipeline that enables application experts without prior experience to leverage it for practical tasks and advance future research in aerial robotics and automated planning.

title: Analyzing the Role of Spinal Joint Dynamics in the Movement of a Sprawling Robot
abstract: Sprawling locomotion in vertebrates, particularly salamanders, illustrates how body undulation and spinal mobility can support stable and efficient movement. Translating these principles to small robotic platforms remains challenging because increasing morphological flexibility also increases the control burden. In this work, we study a simplified salamander-inspired quadruped with four 2-DoF legs and a single active spinal joint. Rather than learning all joint motions end-to-end, we evaluate a hybrid controller in which a Hildebrand-style gait provides structured limb coordination while reinforcement learning controls only the spinal joint. This design reduces the policy search space and improves practical deployability, but also restricts gait flexibility compared with fully learned locomotion policies. Through simulation and hardware experiments, we compare fixed-spine, fully learned, torque-limited, and hybrid spine-actuated controllers on target-directed crawling tasks. Our results show that active spinal control improves forward displacement and rough terrain traversal relative to the fixed-spine Hildebrand baseline, while avoiding some high frequency behaviors observed in unconstrained learned policies. These findings suggest that combining biologically inspired gait priors with low-dimensional learned spinal actuation is a promising but deliberately constrained approach for practical sprawling-robot locomotion.

title: WPMoE: A Reinforcement Learning Method for Motion Control in a Musculoskeletal Robot Via Workspace Partitioning and Mixture of Experts
abstract: Musculoskeletal robots are nowadays widely recognized for their potential to mimic human-like motion and dexterity. However, the control problems caused by the nonlinearity and redundancy of these robots limit their further development. Current research has primarily focused on the motion control of musculoskeletal robots with only 2 degrees of freedom, which is still far from the complexity of the realistic human upper limb. Therefore, this paper aims to address the motion control problem of a highly complicated musculoskeletal upper limb robot with 27 degrees of freedom and 63 muscles-tendon units, focusing on controlling 7 degrees of freedom at the shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints. To realize this goal, WPMoE (Workspace Partitioning and Mixture of Experts) is proposed, which divides the workspace into multiple sub-workspaces and introduces a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture as the controller. To evaluate the effectiveness of WPMoE, experiments are conducted in a simulated environment using the Mujoco physics engine. As shown in the results, WPMoE successfully enables the musculoskeletal robot reach targets accurately with a mean position error of less than 14 mm and shows better performance than baseline methods in terms of control accuracy, policy convergence speed and stability. Therefore, the effectiveness of WPMoE has been demonstrated.

title: Learning Multi-Robot Coordination through Locality-Based Factorized Multi-Agent Actor-Critic Algorithm
abstract: In this work, we present a novel cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning method called Locality based Factorized Multi-Agent Actor-Critic (Loc-FACMAC). Existing state-of-the-art algorithms, such as FACMAC, rely on global reward information, which may not accurately reflect the quality of individual robots' actions in decentralized systems. We integrate the concept of locality into critic learning, where strongly related robots form partitions during training. Robots within the same partition have a greater impact on each other, leading to more precise policy evaluation. Additionally, we construct a dependency graph to capture the relationships between robots, facilitating the partitioning process. This approach mitigates the curse of dimensionality and prevents robots from using irrelevant information. Our method improves existing algorithms by focusing on local rewards and leveraging partition-based learning to enhance training efficiency and performance. We evaluate the performance of Loc-FACMAC in three environments: Hallway, Multi-cartpole, and Bounded-Cooperative-Navigation. We explore the impact of partition sizes on the performance and compare the result with baseline MARL algorithms such as LOMAQ, FACMAC, and QMIX. The experiments reveal that, if the locality structure is defined properly, Loc-FACMAC outperforms these baseline algorithms up to 108%, indicating that exploiting the locality structure in the actor-critic framework improves the MARL performance.

title: Towards Capability-Aware Traversability Navigation for Unstructured Environments
abstract: Estimating traversability in unstructured environments requires conditioning on robot embodiment, as the same terrain can be traversable for one platform and unsafe for another. Existing methods often transfer predictions across morphologies through late-stage trajectory filtering rather than encoding platform constraints in the learned representation. We propose Capability-Aware Traversability (CAT), a framework that embeds physical limits directly into the spatial feature space. CAT grounds dense supervision masks in physical trajectories through an interactive annotation pipeline and modulates semantic terrain maps with robot-specific traversability vectors through Spatially-Adaptive Denormalization (SPADE) blocks. Across human-annotated and trajectory-aligned datasets, CAT leads all ranking-based metrics, improving AUROC by 11.0% on physically executed trajectories and AUPRC by 15.8% on human traces over the strongest baseline. Ablations show that spatial conditioning and per-robot prototypes produce capability sensitivity beyond generic path prediction. Deployments on a legged quadruped and a wheeled skid-steer demonstrate embodiment-aware obstacle avoidance on embedded hardware at 4.8Hz. Project page: capability-aware-traversability.github.io

title: BCF-Map: Bidirectional Cross-Attention Fusion for Robust Multimodal Indoor Semantic Mapping
abstract: Indoor semantic mapping for mobile robots remains highly sensitive to illumination changes and cross-domain transfer, frequently resulting in inconsistent scene predictions and fragmented semantic maps. We propose a lightweight two-stage pipeline that (i) produces per-frame semantic observations via multimodal fusion and (ii) integrates these observations with robot poses to build a 2D semantic map. Our semantic observation model fuses RGB features with an auxiliary geometric representation estimated from RGB images using bidirectional cross-attention, modality projections, and regularizers that promote cross-modal alignment and complementarity, improving robustness under severe appearance changes. We evaluate our approach on two large-scale robotic benchmarks, KTH-IDOL2 and COLD, both structured into multiple subdomains (platforms and laboratories) and illumination conditions (sunny, cloudy, and night). In illumination transfer condition, the proposed Full model achieves 97.34% on KTH-IDOL2 and 97.61% on COLD, improving RGB-only by up to +5.90 points. Under cross-domain transfer condition, it reaches 93.11% on KTH-IDOL2 and 58.53% on COLD, with gains of +8.19 and +8.27 points over RGB-only, respectively. Ablation experiments on challenging data splits demonstrate improvements of up to +10.19 points, highlighting the contribution of each component. Qualitative 2D maps on night-time sequences show improved spatial consistency and fewer incorrect class transitions along robot trajectories.

title: Schur-MI: Fast Mutual Information for Robotic Information Gathering
abstract: Mutual information (MI) is a principled and widely used objective for robotic information gathering (RIG), providing strong theoretical guarantees for sensor placement (SP) and informative path planning (IPP). However, its high computational cost—dominated by repeated log-determinant evaluations—has limited its use in real-time planning. This paper presents Schur-MI, a Gaussian process (GP) MI formulation that (i) leverages the iterative structure of RIG to precompute and reuse expensive intermediate quantities across planning steps, and (ii) uses a Schur-complement factorization to avoid large determinant computations. Together, these methods reduce the per-evaluation cost of MI from O(|V|³) to O(|A|³), where V and A denote the candidate and selected sensing locations, respectively. Experiments on real-world bathymetry datasets show that Schur-MI achieves up to a 12.7× speedup over the standard MI formulation. Field trials with an autonomous surface vehicle (ASV) performing adaptive IPP further demonstrate the method’s practicality. By making MI computation tractable for online planning, Schur-MI helps bridge the gap between information-theoretic objectives and real-time robotic exploration. Our code is available at: www.sgp-tools.com

title: Uncertainty-Aware Auto-Annotation for Multi-Domain 3D Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Generating dense annotations for 3D semantic segmentation is a significant bottleneck on 3D semantic understanding. While recent methods leverage 2D Visual Foundation Models (VFMs) to create 3D pseudo-labels automatically, they suffer from critical noise and systematic errors because they often ignore the underlying uncertainty of the VFMs' predictions. To address this, we propose a novel uncertainty-aware probabilistic framework that explicitly models the uncertainty of each pseudo-label. Our framework represents VFMs predictions as Dirichlet distributions, quantifying uncertainty arising from both insufficient and inconsistent observations, which in turn guides our proposed uncertainty-guided 3D consistency network to prioritize learning from more reliable labels. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on SemanticKITTI and competitive performance on nuScenes datasets for open-vocabulary 3D semantic segmentation, demonstrating the effectiveness of our uncertainty-aware aggregation and training strategy. The source code is available at: https://github.com/Rocense/UASeg.
presentations: Trustworthy Semantic Maps for Robot Exploration

title: Beyond Fixed Goal Delivery: Online POMDP Planning for Target Interception in Crowds
abstract: Target interception in crowded environments requires reaching a moving objective while navigating among multiple uncertain human agents. Since human navigation intent is not directly observable, the robot must reason over multiple possible future interaction outcomes. We formulate interception in crowds as a partially observable Markov decision process and solve it online using tree search under a fixed computational budget. In this setting, the action–space structure directly shapes the search tree and how computational effort is allocated. We perform a controlled comparison between a sequential path–speed planner, which first plans a spatial path and then modulates speed along it, and a unified planner that jointly branches over steering and speed within tree search. Across simulations with up to 200 humans, both approaches perform similarly at low crowd density but diverge sharply as density increases. At the highest crowd density, the sequential planner has a safe–interception rate 31 percentage points lower and requires 44% more time than the unified steering-speed planner, revealing a structural limitation of spatial restriction. Project Webpage: tic-planning.github.io
presentations: Understanding and Navigating Crowded Social Spaces

title: Prox-Nav: Constrained Reinforcement Learning for Safe Social Navigation with Proxemic Constraints
abstract: Mobile robots operating in human-populated environments, such as service robots navigating crowded indoor spaces, must balance task efficiency with explicit safety guarantees. While prior approaches often rely on human trajectory prediction to anticipate collisions, prediction uncertainty can lead either to unsafe behavior or overly conservative motion. In this work, we present Prox-Nav, a constrained reinforcement learning (CRL) framework for safe social navigation with proxemic-inspired safety constraints. Instead of relying on trajectory prediction, we design dense geometric and velocity-based constraints that directly enforce interpersonal safety. To enable stable CRL training across diverse crowd scenarios, we introduce an episode-based automated curriculum learning (ACL) strategy that progressively increases task difficulty according to the number of completed episodes, producing a natural self-paced training process. Training is conducted in a crowd-aware simulation environment with scenario-specific pedestrian behaviors, enabling scalable CRL training and systematic evaluation. Prox-Nav achieves strong safety-efficiency trade-offs, reducing the collision rate to as low as 1.33% while maintaining high task performance. Real-world experiments further demonstrate safe and socially compliant behavior.
presentations: Understanding and Navigating Crowded Social Spaces

title: The SOSI Toolkit: Ontology, Synthetic Dataset, and Benchmark for Social Situation Understanding in Robotics
abstract: Robots operating in human environments must interpret not only physical layouts but also social situations. Decisions such as whether to approach, wait, interrupt, or reroute depend on scene-level social context that is often ambiguous in raw perception. Current systems frequently rely on ad hoc labels and task-specific heuristics, which limit comparability, interpretability, and cumulative progress. This paper introduces SOSI, a neuro-symbolic toolkit for social situation understanding in robotics. SOSI is structured around three coordinated pillars: a formal ontology that defines social situations in machine-readable and compositional terms; an ontology-driven synthetic dataset with explicit labels and controlled variation; and a benchmark protocol based on semantic separability, retrieval, and synthetic-to-real transfer. The presented dataset release is an initial benchmark slice that covers a subset of SOSI dimensions. A CLIP-based contrastive approach is used as an initial baseline for the benchmark. Experiments show stable convergence on synthetic data and improved retrieval performance on real robot observations compared to the base CLIP model. By unifying formal semantics, data generation, and evaluation, SOSI provides reusable infrastructure for rigorous and explainable social situation modeling in robotics.
presentations: Understanding and Navigating Crowded Social Spaces

title: Trajectory-Aware Monocular Relative Pose Estimation for Cooperative UAVs: From Geometric Optimization to Hybrid Learning
abstract: Accurate relative pose estimation is a core require- ment for cooperative multi-UAV autonomy. While monocular cameras are attractive for resource-constrained aerial platforms due to their low weight and power consumption, bearing- only measurements render depth and orientation recovery underconstrained without additional structure. We reinterpret this as a motion-conditioned observability design problem: by deliberately engineering the target UAV’s trajectory, motion itself becomes the primary geometric constraint. Planar trajec- tories induce angular ambiguity and ill-conditioned estimation, whereas sustained three-dimensional excitation resolves this degeneracy without fiducial markers or known target geom- etry. To exploit this insight, we develop three complementary frameworks: (i) a trajectory-aware geometric optimizer based on Levenberg–Marquardt refinement, (ii) a Transformer-based estimator mapping image-plane trajectory sequences directly to relative pose, and (iii) a hybrid coarse-to-fine pipeline in which the learned model selects the physically consistent solution basin before geometric refinement. Three-dimensional trajec- tories reduce yaw error by more than an order of magnitude for learning-based estimation and eliminate ambiguity-driven failures in the hybrid framework. The hybrid framework elim- inates catastrophic convergence failures while achieving over three orders of magnitude in computational speedup. Limited real-world flight experiments further demonstrate practical feasibility.
presentations: Visual-Inertial State Estimation for Agile Flight

title: Energy-Aware Morphing: Adaptive Curriculum-Based DRL for Obstacle Traversal in Transformable Wheeled-Legged Robots
abstract: Transformable wheeled-legged robots excel in unstructured environments but struggle to balance traversability with energy efficiency. Existing Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) methods prioritize kinematic feasibility, yielding high-energy behaviors that fail to transfer to physical platforms due to unmodeled actuator dynamics. To bridge this gap, we propose an energy-aware DRL framework with two key innovations. First, a Global Energy Allocation Reward function explicitly optimizes the ``Energy Return on Investment'' to prevent myopic motion planning. Second, a Policy Uncertainty-based Adaptive Curriculum Learning (ACL) strategy dynamically adjusts training difficulty based on policy entropy to ensure stable convergence. We validate the proposed framework based on a custom-built transformable robot, demonstrating successful Sim-to-Real transfer. Real-world experiments on step climbing and narrow passage traversal show that our method reduces energy consumption by up to 25.8% and traversal time by up to 13.4% compared to strong baselines. The framework generates deployable, energy-efficient policies suitable for long-endurance autonomous missions.

title: CEER: Compliant End-Effector and Root Control As a Unified Interface for Hierarchical Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
abstract: Humanoid robots have achieved impressive locomotion capabilities, yet integrating contact-rich manipulation with hierarchical task planning remains challenging. Most existing approaches rely on joint-space motion tracking, which is difficult to interpret and tightly coupled to specific planners. We propose CEER, a compliant end-effector and root (EE-root) control abstraction for humanoid loco-manipulation. By operating in an interpretable task space defined by root motion commands and end-effector pose targets, CEER enables compliance-aware whole-body control while remaining compatible with heterogeneous high-level planners. A teacher–student framework is adopted to distill a general motion-tracking controller into a low-level policy that consumes only EE-root commands. We further construct a hierarchical three-layer system in which diverse mid-level skills and planners produce unified EE-root commands without retraining the whole-body controller. Experiments in simulation and on hardware demonstrate accurate end-effector tracking, contact-rich manipulation behaviors, and long-horizon task execution within a room-scale environment. These results suggest that compliant EE-root control provides a practical abstraction layer for modular humanoid loco-manipulation.

title: Olaf: Bringing an Animated Character to Life in the Physical World
abstract: Animated characters often move in non-physical ways and have proportions that are far from a typical walking robot. This provides an ideal platform for innovation in both mechanical design and stylized motion control. In this paper, we bring Olaf to life in the physical world, relying on reinforcement learning guided by animation references for control. To create the illusion of Olaf's feet moving along his body, we hide two asymmetric legs under a soft foam skirt. To fit actuators inside the character, we use spherical and planar linkages in the arms, mouth, and eyes. Because the walk cycle results in harsh contact sounds, we introduce additional rewards that noticeably reduce impact noise. The large head, driven by small actuators in the character's slim neck, creates a risk of overheating, amplified by the costume. To keep actuators from overheating, we feed temperature values as additional inputs to policies, introducing new rewards to keep them within bounds. We validate the efficacy of our modeling in simulation and through experiments on the robot.
presentations: Whole-Body Control for Novel Robot Behaviors

title: De-Ghosting Depth: Mitigating Spatio-Temporal Misalignment Via Drivable Area Constraints
abstract: Depth completion densifies sparse LiDAR measurements with RGB guidance and is fundamental to 3D perception in autonomous systems. In dynamic environments, the intrinsic spatio-temporal asynchrony between scanning LiDARs and cameras induces cross-modal misalignment, resulting in severe depth ghosting artifacts. To mitigate it, we propose a novel dynamics-aware depth completion framework built upon drivable area constraints. Our approach is motivated by the observation that dynamic objects typically manifest as outliers relative to the planar manifold of the drivable surface. We first introduce a geometry-consistent segmentation module that refines Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) masks using strictly defined geometric planar constraints. Leveraging these reliable drivable area masks, we propose an ``Extract-Relocate-Filter" (ERF) strategy that separates motion-induced outliers, extracts dynamic objects via seeded region growing, and relocates misaligned point clouds by maximizing non-drivable area overlap. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks and a challenging self-collected dataset demonstrate that our method effectively suppresses ghosting artifacts and consistently improves dynamic depth consistency across multiple depth completion backbones.

title: PolarDepth: Polarization-Guided Monocular Depth for Visual Odometry
abstract: Glass surfaces remain challenging for indoor robot perception. Depth sensors and RGB-only monocular depth estimation often fail because of reflections, refractions, and low-texture regions. To this end, we present PolarDepth, a polarization-enhanced monocular depth framework for glass-dominant environments. We utilize a single polarization sensor to obtain a standard RGB image and a three-channel encoding of polarization cues, designed to be compatible with RGB-trained foundation depth models, and which we call Polar-RGB. This representation enables recovery of structure in transparent and specular regions where RGB cues are unreliable. We predict depth from both the RGB and Polar-RGB representations and fuse the predictions using a learned per-pixel reliability gate for mid-level fusion, highlighting RGB in diffuse regions and polarization on reflective surfaces. We demonstrate improvements in depth estimation and visual odometry performance over RGB-only baselines in glass-walled corridors on both real-world and synthetic data.

title: SV-RCNN: Robust Structural-Encoded Voxel Features for 3D Object Detection on Sparse Point Clouds
abstract: 3D object detection in LiDAR point clouds faces significant challenges in sparse point clouds and unfamiliar environments. Existing methods often rely on simple multi-layer perceptrons or normalization techniques, limiting robustness in real-world settings, particularly for small or irregular objects. This work presents Structural Voxel RCNN (SV-RCNN), a generalizable 3D object detector that encodes geometric structure within each voxel through a structural convolutional operation. SV-RCNN introduces a learnable receptive field that adapts to object scale and sparsity, enabling reliable detection under varying conditions. Experimental results across multiple datasets demonstrate that SV-RCNN improves cross-domain performance and maintains strong accuracy without requiring additional adaptation steps. These results highlight the importance of structural encoding in enhancing generalization for real-world applications.

title: Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation for Dynamic 3D Scenes Using Scene Flow Estimation
abstract: 3D open-vocabulary semantic segmentation has shown great potential in applications such as autonomous driving and mixed reality. However, achieving accurate segmentation in dynamic environments remains challenging due to motion-induced inconsistencies. To address this issue, we incorporate scene flow as temporal information into a static semantic backbone to enhance semantic consistency and accuracy over time. Our method captures inter-frame motion cues from point cloud sequences and leverages them, together with a local clustering mechanism, to refine semantic label consistency in consecutive frames. Furthermore, we introduce a two-way scene flow-based data augmentation strategy that exploits both forward and backward motion to jointly train the model in bidirectional temporal contexts. On the large-scale nuScenes autonomous driving dataset, our method achieves a 0.4% overall improvement in hIoU and a 2.37% gain under high-motion scenes. On the synthetic object-centric dataset, it achieves a 4.53% overall hIoU improvement and a 6.09% gain in high-motion scenes, while reducing the ID switch rate by 0.5%.

title: TriLift: Interpolation-Free Tri-Plane Lifting for Efficient 3D Perception on Embedded Systems
abstract: Dense 3D convolutions provide high accuracy for perception but are too computationally expensive for real-time robotic systems. Existing tri-plane methods rely on 2D image features with interpolation, point-wise queries, and implicit MLPs, which makes them computationally heavy and unsuitable for embedded 3D inference. As an alternative, we propose a novel interpolation-free tri-plane lifting and volumetric fusion framework, that directly projects 3D voxels into plane features and reconstructs a feature volume through broadcast and summation. This shifts nonlinearity to 2D convolutions, reducing complexity while remaining fully parallelizable. To mitigate spatial information loss inherent in projections, we incorporate a lightweight adaptive positional encoding module that helps bridge the spatial information gap, dynamically recovering fine geometric details with negligible overhead. To capture global context, we add a low-resolution volumetric branch fused with the lifted features through a lightweight integration layer, yielding a design that is both efficient and end-to-end GPU-accelerated. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, we conduct experiments on classification, completion, segmentation, and detection, and we map the trade-off between efficiency and accuracy across tasks. Results show that classification and completion retain or improve accuracy, while segmentation and detection show a trade-off, significantly reducing computational demand with only a slight decrease in accuracy. On-device benchmarks on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin nano confirm robust real-time throughput, demonstrating the suitability of the approach for embedded robotic perception.
keywords: Embedded Systems for Robotic and Automation

title: Recti-Q: Feature-Space Rectification for Out-Of-Distribution-Robust Quantized Perception in Edge Robotics
abstract: Robotic perception pipelines increasingly rely on large vision backbones deployed on SWaP-constrained edge platforms, making post-training quantization (PTQ) attractive for real-time inference. However, while PTQ often preserves clean in-distribution accuracy, we show that it can substantially degrade reliability under deployment-relevant distribution shifts (e.g., sensor noise, severe weather, and novel operating environments), creating a Quantization-Induced Robustness Gap. Across foundational vision benchmarks (ImageNet-C and PACS), 4-bit PTQ models exhibit pronounced robustness degradation despite negligible ID accuracy loss. To address this, we propose Recti-Q, a lightweight feature-space rectification framework that freezes the quantized backbone and trains a small classifier-head LoRA adapter using only source data. Recti-Q is architecture-agnostic across CNNs and Transformers, supports efficient teacher-free training, and recovers a significant portion of the lost robustness, in some cases matching or exceeding FP32 performance. At less than 1% parameter overhead (as small as 6 KB), Recti-Q preserves over 99% of PTQ memory savings, adds negligible compute, and enables low-bandwidth Over-The-Air (OTA) resilience patching for deployed robotic fleets operating in unpredictable physical environments.

title: 3D Open-Vocabulary Detection Via Visual Alignment and Generative Captions
abstract: Open-vocabulary 3D object detection remains a significant challenge for outdoor scenes, with existing methods often struggling to effectively transfer the rich semantic knowledge from powerful 2D Vision-Language Models (VLMs) into a 3D context. We propose a novel, two-part framework for this task. First, we introduce a direct, object-level distillation method. We generate class-agnostic 3D proposals to source regions from the entire scene, without relying on any manual labels. We leverage a spatially-aware VLM to extract a semantic embedding from each proposal’s projected 2D bounding box and supervise our 3D model to predict this embedding on a per- instance basis. Second, to enhance zero-shot capability and inject domain-specific information, we employ a powerful Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) as an image captioner to generate rich textual captions for each of these proposals. These captions are integrated into the training objective to directly align the 3D features with these rich semantics, creating a composite loss that combines direct feature distillation with caption-based semantic enrichment. Our experiments validate the effectiveness of our approach, establishing a new state of the art in 3D open-vocabulary detection on the Waymo Open Dataset and nuScenes.

title: A Simple Recipe for Leveraging Dual Foundation Models in Domain Generalised Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Domain generalised semantic segmentation (DGSS) is important for practical applications, such as autonomous driving, where it frequently encounters shifts in weather and geography. Large-scale pretrained models have shown robustness in feature extraction and understanding, making them a strong foundation for DGSS. However, most existing methods rely on a single pretrained backbone, overlooking the complementary features between distinct pretrained algorithms, such as Vision Language Models (VLMs) and Vision Foundation Models (VFMs). Prior studies have attempted to ensemble VLMs and VFMs using token fusion, such as Attention or Mamba, but often incur unnecessary complexity or limited effectiveness. In this work, we rethink the collaboration between pretrained models and propose a simple yet effective gating-based fusion framework that adaptively regulates the token contributions of VLMs and VFMs at the token level. This perspective shifts the collaboration between the two models from direct token fusion (e.g., Attention or Mamba) to gating interaction, where tokens from both models interact only to learn the gating weights. Interestingly, this simple gating mechanism surpasses Attention and Mamba architectures, achieving 68.89 IoU on synthetic-to-real and 72.94 IoU on real-to-real benchmark. Code is available at https://github.com/RuoyuGuo/GI-Adapter.
presentations: Adapting Detection and Segmentation to New Settings

title: IAST: Instance Augmentation and Self-Training for Domain Adaptation on 3D Object Detection
abstract: 3D LiDAR object detection suffers severe perfor- mance degradation under cross-domain shift, especially when sensor configurations (e.g., LiDAR beams) differ. Gradual do- main adaptation (GDA) mitigates this via intermediate domains and self-training, but remains limited by inefficient knowledge transfer, incomplete intermediate data, and noisy pseudo-labels. We propose Instance Augmentation Self-training (IAST), a semi-supervised domain adaptation framework for 3D point cloud detection. With scarce target labels, IAST inserts target instances into source backgrounds to build intermediate-domain samples that preserve geometric and semantic integrity. A dynamic weighting scheme then jointly pre-trains on source, intermediate, and target data for progressive domain transfer. During self-training, pseudo-labels on unlabeled target data are refined by a vision-language model (VLM) to suppress low-quality supervision. Experiments on Waymo and nuScenes show that IAST achieves 59.92 mAP (N→W) and 54.22 mAP (W→N), out-performing the best baselines by 4.33 and 2.54 mAP, respectively.

title: FreqKD: Distillation-Based Single Domain Generalization Via Frequency-Structured Knowledge Transfer
abstract: Robust object detection under domain shift remains a critical challenge for autonomous systems operating in dynamic real-world environments. While recent single-domain generalization (SDG) methods rely on complex consistency regularization and auxiliary training modules, they often incur high computational overhead and implementation complexity. In this work, we reformulate single-domain generalization as a representation-level knowledge transfer problem and propose a distillation-based SDG framework that enables efficient and robust learning without auxiliary domain generalization modules. Our key insight is that high-frequency components encode domain-invariant structural information that remains stable across environmental variations. Instead of enforcing prediction-level consistency under augmentation, we transfer frequency-structured knowledge at the representation level from a powerful teacher trained on clean images to a lightweight student trained on augmented data. Specifically, we introduce a frequency-structured distillation objective that aligns high-frequency representations in the Fourier domain, together with a prototype-level semantic alignment mechanism that preserves instance-level consistency. This paradigm shift—from prediction-level consistency to representation-level structural transfer—allows us to discard contrastive heads, random proposals, and JSD-based regularization used in prior work. Extensive experiments on Cityscapes-C and the Diverse Weather Dataset demonstrate that a lightweight student achieves competitive or superior corruption robustness compared to its heavier teacher under unseen domain conditions, while reducing student-side training time by 47%. These results highlight that domain generalization can be effectively achieved through structured knowledge transfer rather than augmentation-driven consistency learning.

title: CoLoRA: Optimal Transport Meets LoRA for Multi-Domain Open-Vocabulary Segmentation
abstract: Robust robotic perception is essential for em- bodied AI applications, enabling autonomous systems such as ground vehicles and drones to accurately interpret and navi- gate complex environments. These applications span a broad spectrum of domains, ranging from specialized areas such as medical imaging, remote sensing, drone-based monitoring, autonomous driving, agriculture, and engineering to broader real-world scenarios, including maritime operations. A major challenge in these systems is achieving semantic understanding of previously unseen categories, which is addressed by open- vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS). OVSS leverages large-scale vision–language models like CLIP to assign pixel- level labels based on textual descriptions. However, existing models often struggle to generalize across domains, limiting their effectiveness in real-world, multi-domain settings. To address these limitations, we propose CoLoRA, a novel prompt learning framework that combines two key components: Cost- Aware Optimal Transport via Aggregation (COAT) and LoRA adaptation applied at model convergence. Evaluated across 19 multi-domain datasets, CoLoRA achieves state-of-the-art performance, producing a more generalizable OVSS model while adding only a marginal increase in parameters compared to the baseline. Moreover, it consistently outperforms existing methods across diverse domains. The source code is available at https://aniruddhsikdar1.github.io/publications/colora/.
presentations: Adapting Detection and Segmentation to New Settings

title: Foundation-Assisted Active Learning for Object Detection Annotation
abstract: The annotation cost for remote sensing object detection is high, while existing active learning methods still face several challenges in object detection scenarios, including the coupling of localization and classification uncertainty, severe localization noise in the cold-start stage, and pseudo-diversity caused by high-recall candidate proposals. To address these issues, we propose a foundation-model-collaborative active learning and semi-automatic annotation framework for efficient construction of remote sensing object detection datasets. We build a dual-source mechanism consisting of a reference localization source (SA-source) based on UPN+SAM2 and a detector prediction source (OD-source), and further propose a Foundation-model-enhanced Dual-Source Uncertainty estimation to improve sample selection quality in the cold-start stage by jointly modeling localization consistency and classification confidence. Furthermore, we propose Object-Centric Diversity Sampling, which constructs object-level representations using DINOv2 features and SAM2 masks to improve sample coverage while suppressing pseudo-diversity. To address geometric noise in the semi-automatic annotation stage, we design Dual-Source Box Switching, which replaces noisy detector boxes with matched refined boxes from the SA-source, thereby reducing the manual burden of box refinement. Experiments on DIOR, HRSC2016, DOTAv2, and FAIR1M show that our method achieves superior or comparable results under most annotation budgets, with notably stronger cold-start sample efficiency in the low-budget regime.

title: Learning to Segment Liquids in Real-World Images
abstract: Liquids like water, wine and medicine are everywhere. However, limited attention has been given to the task of segmenting liquids, hindering the ability of robots to safely avoid and interact with them. The segmentation of liquids is difficult because liquids come in diverse appearances and shapes; moreover, they can be both transparent or reflective, taking on arbitrary objects and scenes from their background and surroundings. To take on this challenge, we construct a liquid dataset, LQDS, consisting of 5000 real-world images annotated into 14 distinct classes, and design a novel liquid detection model, LQDM, which leverages cross-attention between a dedicated boundary branch and the main segmentation branch to enhance mask predictions. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of LQDM on the testing set of LQDS, outperforming state-of-the-art methods to establish a strong baseline for the semantic segmentation of liquids. We believe that LQDS and LQDM will facilitate future research in liquid segmentation and enable practical applications in robotics. Our dataset and code is released at https://lonaslee.github.io/LQDM/.

title: Learning Continuous Obstacle-Rich Pursuit for Drone Swarms
abstract: Autonomous pursuit of multiple drones in cluttered environments is challenging due to complex obstacle distributions, evolving adversary behaviors, and strong non-stationarity in multi-agent interactions. Agents trained with conventional reinforcement learning methods often fail to learn effective policies in such settings, as strong adversarial opponents can suppress learning signals and destabilize training. This paper proposes a novel dual-stabilized asynchronous multi-stage deep reinforcement learning framework (DAM-DRL) for pursuit-evasion games. The proposed approach adopts a progressive multi-stage training scheme to control the growth of adversarial strength, preventing either side of the adversarial agents from becoming overly dominant within a single stage. At each stage, a group of adversarial agents is frozen while the opposing group is trained, and the trained policies are subsequently merged to initialize the next stage. Inspired by Nash equilibrium, DAM-DRL stabilizes adversarial learning by limiting unilateral policy improvement and empirically produces stronger policies than competing methods. Extensive simulation experiments demonstrate that our approach improves pursuit and obstacle avoidance performance compared to representative baselines in obstacle-rich environments with strong adversarial agents. In addition, physical experiments are conducted to further verify that effective policies can be deployed in real flights.

title: Topological Online Learning for Displacement-based Formation Control
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of robust formation control by introducing Topological Online Learning for Displacement-based (TOLD) formation control, a real-time edge-level adaptation framework. Unlike conventional node-level robust controllers that regulate individual robot inputs without modifying the interaction topology, TOLD updates the interaction topology weights online to directly minimize formation distortion. Two strategies are proposed under the TOLD formation control framework: Online Gradient Flow (OGF) with unconstrained weights and Online Exponential Gradient Flow (OExpGF) with non-negative convex weights. Theoretical analysis establishes that, for single-integrator agents over directed graphs, OExpGF guarantees asymptotic consensus, while OGF ensures bounded formation distortion. Simulations with twelve robots under intermittent disturbances show 1.2%–33.14% median cumulative Root Mean Distortion Error reduction when augmenting TOLD with node-level controllers. Hardware experiments with Crazyflie 2.0 quadrotors demonstrate over 62% (OGF) and 31.4% (OExpGF) reduction in median formation distortion compared to fixed-weight consensus.

title: COLMAR: Cooperative View Policy Learning for Multi-Agent Active 3D Reconstruction
abstract: Active 3D reconstruction requires selecting informative viewpoints under limited sensing budgets. In multi-agent settings, coordination inefficiencies such as redundant observations and spatial clustering can significantly reduce reconstruction quality. We present COLMAR, a cooperative view policy learning framework for multi-agent active 3D reconstruction. COLMAR formulates viewpoint allocation as a shared policy optimization over map-centric observations and introduces a reconstruction-aware objective that promotes overlap-aware coverage, team-level discovery, and collision-safe exploration. Dense feedback derived from incremental reconstruction updates aligns exploration behavior with downstream geometric quality. The policy is trained using parameter-sharing Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with decentralized execution, enabling scalable deployment without explicit inter-agent communication at inference time. At test time, the learned policy drives 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) for high-fidelity reconstruction. Experiments on GLEAM and Replica demonstrate consistent improvements over heuristic and non-cooperative baselines, achieving up to 54% higher reconstruction accuracy and 49% greater coverage under matched sensing budgets.

title: AutoAresti: A Benchmark and Architecture for Real-Time Aerobatic Sequence Interpretation
abstract: Interpreting multivariate time-series data from dynamic physical environments remains a challenge for autonomous systems, in part due to the lack of open-source, expertly labeled datasets. We address this gap by introducing AerobaticsDB, the first publicly available machine learning dataset for aircraft aerobatics, comprising 284 labeled Aresti-notated maneuvers captured in both real-world (Pitts S2B) and simulated (Zivko Edge 540) aircraft. Aerobatic sequences present a demanding testbed for time-series models: maneuvers vary substantially in duration, transitions between them occur within fractions of a second, and the combinatorial space of valid maneuver sequences is vast. We leverage AerobaticsDB using AutoAresti, a Patch Transformer architecture with a custom training and evaluation pipeline for joint real-time segmentation and recognition of rapidly performed aerobatic sequences. We validate our approach through a rigorous flight test campaign. Our results demonstrate that AutoAresti modestly outperforms (macro-F1 85.8%) recurrent neural-network baselines despite their strong inductive bias for time series applications, while offering superior late-maneuver consistency. Together, AerobaticsDB and AutoAresti provide a new benchmark and baseline for real-time interpretation of dynamic inertial sequences.

title: From Grid to Ring: A New Convolutional Paradigm for Arbitrary-Scale UAV Thermal Super-Resolution
abstract: Arbitrary-scale thermal super-resolution (SR) has emerged as a promising solution to overcome the limitations posed by the low resolution of thermal images, particularly in applications that demand flexible resolution enhancement on unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) platforms. Due to the absence of semantic and color cues in thermal images, the model ability to extract texture representation is crucial for recovering fine details in thermal SR. Considering that thermal images captured by UAV exhibit rich and ring-like texture structures at object boundaries, we introduce Ring Convolution (RingConv), a novel ring-shaped convolution specifically designed to capture such peripheral and texture-dominant patterns. Unlike conventional convolutions that treat all spatial positions equally, RingConv selectively emphasizes precise texture regions to better enhance structural fidelity. Built upon RingConv, we further propose RingSRNet, a new backbone tailored for arbitrary-scale thermal SR that achieves accurate image reconstruction, eliminating the need for complex attention modules. Moreover, a thermal SR dataset (TSR100K) is constructed with a thermal imaging-equipped UAV, comprising 100,000 images collected across a wide range of real-world environments. Finally, extensive experiments conducted on the TSR100K and public datasets demonstrate that RingSRNet consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across various scales, delivering superior results in both visual quality and quantitative metrics.

title: FALCON: Future-Aware Learning with Contextual Object-Centric Pretraining for UAV Action Recognition
abstract: We introduce FALCON, a unified self-supervised video pretraining framework tailored for UAV-based robotics that enables efficient action recognition from raw RGB aerial footage without additional preprocessing at inference. UAV videos are dominated by large, cluttered backgrounds, causing conventional reconstruction-based pretraining to waste capacity on uninformative regions. FALCON addresses this challenge by learning from what matters and what comes next: it combines object-aware masked autoencoding with object-centric future reconstruction, where the model reconstructs future frames but focuses the generative objective only on object regions. Concretely, FALCON incorporates (1) an object-aware masking strategy that preserves informative object-related patches, (2) an object-aware reconstruction loss that mitigates background- dominated bias, and (3) a future reconstruction objective restricted to object regions to inject anticipatory temporal supervision while remaining robust to noisy aerial context. In practice, FALCON achieves superior action recognition accuracy on UAV benchmarks, improving top-1 accuracy by 2.9% on NEC-Drone and 5.8% on UAV-Human with a ViT-B model, while delivering 2×–5× faster inference than supervised methods requiring heavy test-time augmentation.

title: SoraNav: Adaptive UAV Task-Centric Navigation Via Zero-Shot VLM Reasoning
abstract: Autonomous navigation under natural language instructions represents a crucial step toward embodied intelligence, enabling complex task execution in environments ranging from industrial facilities to domestic spaces. However, language-driven 3D navigation for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) requires precise spatial reasoning, a capability inherently lacking in current zero-shot Vision-Language Models (VLMs), which often generate ambiguous outputs and cannot guarantee geometric feasibility. Furthermore, existing Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) methods are predominantly tailored for ground robots with ground-plane planning (2.5D), and cannot generalize to the 3D reasoning required for aerial tasks in small-scale, cluttered environments. In this paper, we present SoraNav, a novel framework enabling zero-shot VLM reasoning for UAV task-centric navigation. To address the spatial-semantic gap, we introduce Multi-modal Visual Annotation (MVA), which encodes 3D geometric priors directly into the VLM's 2D visual input. To mitigate hallucinated or infeasible commands, we propose an Adaptive Decision Making (ADM) strategy that validates VLM proposals against exploration history, seamlessly switching to geometry-based exploration to avoid dead-ends and redundant revisits. Deployed on a custom PX4-based micro-UAV, SoraNav demonstrates robust real-world performance. Quantitative results show our approach significantly outperforms representative baselines, increasing Success Rate (SR) by 25.7% and navigation efficiency (SPL) by 17.3% in 2.5D scenarios, and improving by 39.3% (SR) and 24.7% (SPL) in complex 3D scenarios.

title: Featherlight Flyers: Mastering Cluttered Environments with Minimalistic Sensing and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Flapping-wing Micro Aerial Vehicles (FWMAVs) offer high agility and bio-inspired flight, enabling applications in environments where conventional quadrotors struggle. Reinforcement learning (RL) has recently shown great promise for collision-free autonomous navigation, yet the strict payload and computational limitations of FWMAVs make traditional approaches based on cameras or heavy onboard computation impractical. In this work, we propose a minimalistic obstacle-avoidance framework for FWMAVs that leverages lightweight multizone time-of-flight (ToF) sensors combined with recurrent Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). We employ a state estimation model that infers velocity and position from body attitude dynamics without odometry. Experiments in simulation demonstrate that our RL-based approach outperforms state-of-the-art handcrafted ToF-based baselines and even surpasses vision-based methods in some scenarios. Furthermore, we validate the method in real-world experiments with a modified Flapper Nimble+ robot.

title: LNN-Fly: Continuous-Time UAV Navigation for Robust Obstacle Avoidance under Timing Mismatch
abstract: End-to-end unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) navigation can achieve impressive agility in simulation, yet its obstacle-avoidance behavior often degrades after deployment because the policy must tolerate simulator mismatch, sensing irregularity, and variable-rate control. These effects are especially dangerous in cluttered environments, where stale observations or short control irregularities can directly lead to collisions. We present LNN-Fly, a deployment-oriented continuous-time navigation policy for LiDAR-based UAV obstacle avoidance. The policy combines a dynamic-programming-inspired structured recurrent update, explicit conditioning on the elapsed control interval Δt, and an input-driven adaptive forgetting gate that refreshes stale latent state near hazards while preserving consistency during sustained maneuvers. It is trained with differentiable rollouts that incorporate deployment-relevant sensing and timing perturbations. In simulation, LNN-Fly improves obstacle-avoidance performance in the tested settings and shows better tolerance to reduced control frequency, sparse observations, and control-period jitter. It also transfers zero-shot from a simplified differentiable simulator to a physical quadrotor. In indoor cross-frequency real-world tests, the system achieves 100% success over 20 flights, while policy inference has a median latency of 0.514 ms on a desktop graphics processing unit (GPU) and about 2.5 ms on the onboard central processing unit (CPU), with onboard P95 latency below 30 ms.

title: ChunkFlow: Towards Continuity-Consistent Chunked Policy Learning
abstract: Vision–language action (VLA) models increasingly adopt chunked action heads to satisfy real-time constraints; however, this introduces boundary jitter: overlapping regions between consecutive chunks often yield inconsistent predictions, degrading temporal coherence and the task success rate. Existing methods, such as inference-time blending, merely reweight mismatched proposals without correcting underlying errors, leading to residual accumulation under biased or noisy histories. We propose ChunkFlow, a seam-aware training-and-execution framework for chunked policies that aligns chunk structure with boundary execution. It partitions each chunk into frozen, editable, and future zones, applies deterministic overlap blending at execution, and trains raw predictions with seam and first- and second-order continuity losses. History corruption and scheduled sampling improve robustness to executed-history errors, while an AWAC fine-tuning stage adapts the policy without removing these structural regularizers. Under mild smoothness assumptions, pre-blending seam discrepancies provably decay with increasing overlap. Experiments on CALVIN, LIBERO, and real robots show an improved success-stability trade-off with low-latency inference. Project page: https://cytoderm-ai.github.io/chunkflow.
presentations: Advancing Policy Learning for Robotic Manipulation

title: Self-Curriculum Model-Based Reinforcement Learning for Shape Control of Deformable Linear Objects
abstract: Precise shape control of Deformable Linear Objects (DLOs) is crucial in robotic applications such as industrial and medical fields. However, existing methods face challenges in handling complex large deformation tasks, especially those involving opposite curvatures, and lack efficiency and precision. To address this, we propose a two-stage framework combining Reinforcement Learning (RL) and online visual servoing. In the large-deformation stage, a model-based reinforcement learning approach using an ensemble of dynamics models is introduced to significantly improve sample efficiency. Additionally, we design a self-curriculum goal generation mechanism that dynamically selects intermediate-difficulty goals with high diversity through imagined evaluations, thereby optimizing the policy learning process. In the small-deformation stage, a Jacobian-based visual servo controller is deployed to ensure high-precision convergence. Simulation results show that the proposed method enables efficient policy learning and significantly outperforms mainstream baselines in shape control success rate and precision. Furthermore, the framework effectively transfers the policy trained in simulation to real-world tasks with zero-shot adaptation. It successfully completes all 30 cases with diverse initial and target shapes across DLOs of different sizes and materials. The project website will be accessible upon acceptance.

title: SynthLA: Synthetic Language–Action Multi–task Policies for Zero–shot Real–world Manipulation Via Structured Perception
abstract: We introduce SynthLA, a modular approach for learning a low-level language-action policy without real-world robot demonstrations or control primitives. We adapt a large language model (LLM) into a language-action policy, given a structured text representing the environment and robot states. During training, we generate millions of synthetic state-action pairs for multiple tasks, leveraging rule-based natural language generation (NLG) of randomized environments. At deployment time, a vision model estimates the environment state from RGB-D observations, and formatted as structured text. We evaluate SynthLA on four real-world tabletop tasks (lift, pick&place, move, close-the-pot) against SOTA VLAs and LLM planners, showing improvements in success rate while relying only on synthetic training data. In the systematic evaluation, we demonstrate that our approach is robust to out-of-distribution object manipulation and dynamic environments, capable of learning new tasks incrementally, and generalizes to unseen objects and task instructions.

title: Prior Reinforce: Goal-Conditioned Dynamic Manipulation with Limited Trials
abstract: Embodied robots have achieved strong performance in many real-world manipulation tasks, yet agile dynamic manipulation remains challenging due to high sensitivity to motion parameters and sparse outcome-level feedback. Tasks such as shooting a basketball into a hoop require precise control of fast open-loop motions, where small trajectory variations can lead to large outcome deviations, making data-efficient adaptation difficult for existing methods that rely on large-scale interaction, reward engineering, or accurate dynamic modeling. We propose Prior Reinforce (P.R.), a simple and practical framework for goal-conditioned dynamic manipulation. The method first learns a structured motion manifold from a small set of demonstrations using a conditional diffusion model, and then adapts motions toward new goals through feedback-driven optimization in a low-dimensional condition space. By separating motion generation from outcome-driven adaptation, the framework enables efficient refinement using only a small number of real-world trials under noisy perception. Experiments on multiple real-world dynamic manipulation tasks demonstrate that P.R. reliably achieves new goals within as few as ten total trials while remaining robust to perception noise and hardware uncertainty, suggesting a practical approach for low-trial real-world robot adaptation.

title: Jointly Learning Predicates and Actions Enables Zero-Shot Skill Composition
abstract: Learning from Demonstration (LfD) enables robots to learn complex behaviors from expert examples, yet existing approaches often fail to generalize to new compositions of known skills without retraining. Modern generative policies model distributions over action trajectories alone, and thus are unable to reason about the symbolic outcomes required for robust composition. We propose that skills should jointly model action trajectories and the symbolic outcomes they induce. To address this gap, we introduce Predicate-Action Skills (Pacts), a class of closed-loop visuomotor policies that model skills as a joint generative process over action and predicate belief trajectories, producing coherent action–outcome rollouts within a single model. Jointly generating actions and predicates enables Pacts to learn internal representations that improve both action generation and predicate classification, outperforming action-only policies and standalone predicate predictors. Furthermore, we demonstrate zero-shot composition of learned skills via planning by leveraging online predicate predictions from Pacts as a symbolic interface for sequencing and monitoring execution.

title: MaskVLA: Visual Masking against Trajectory Overfitting of Vision-Language-Action Model
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models integrate vision-language understanding with executable robot actions, enabling end-to-end learning for robot control. However, our empirical analysis reveals that existing models exhibit severe trajectory overfitting when finetuned on limited datasets. To guide the model in effectively utilizing wrist camera information, we propose MaskVLA, a masking-based fine-tuning strategy. By randomly masking a small portion of the main camera’s visual information, the model is guided to autonomously learn more fine-grained, task-relevant, and effective visual features. This process leads to the emergence of robust policies, thereby enhancing the model’s capability to tackle complex manipulation tasks and improving its generalization performance. Our method has been comprehensively evaluated on RoboTwin 2.0, achieving an average success rate improvement of 23.2% and 16.8% compared to pi_0 and OpenVLA-OFT, respectively. Furthermore, experiments on real-world ALOHA robots also demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

title: RobustFuzz: A Semantic Disturbance Benchmark for Learned Policies in Embodied Control
abstract: Learned control policies enable impressive embodied agents, yet deployment reliability is limited by temporally structured semantic hardware disturbances such as actuator-bus jitter, asynchronous command updates, and bursty sensor dropouts. Existing benchmarks often emphasize task generalization or i.i.d. corruptions while under-modeling the timing faults that dominate cyber-physical deployments. We present RobustFuzz, a semantic fuzzing benchmark that actively searches for failure-inducing disturbance schedules within a hardware-informed disturbance space. Inspired by feedback-driven fuzzing, RobustFuzz prioritizes disturbance seeds by proprioceptive coverage gain and concentrates sampling near collapse frontiers where policies transition sharply from success to catastrophic failure. Across H1, Aloha, and Franka in Isaac Gym, RobustFuzz reveals substantial robustness gaps under physically plausible timing disturbances, achieving 1.88--1.93x higher collapse rates than domain randomization across all three platforms. We implement an observation-stream proxy for packet-loss-induced control blindness and fit conservative timing-irregularity bounds from ROS 2 telemetry measurements. We release disturbance schemas and realized schedules for exact replay. On H1, RobustFuzz achieves a 1.92x higher collapse rate, 37.2% vs. 19.4% for DR, and uncovers more diverse failure clusters, 10 vs. 4.

title: CAMFlow: Learning Coordination-Aware Aerial Manipulation Via Consistency Flow Matching
abstract: Deploying generative visuomotor policies on aerial manipulators remains constrained by the platform's underactuated dynamics, which demand high-frequency control to maintain flight stability. However, standard diffusion models suffer from high inference latency, limiting their use on highly dynamic aerial systems. Moreover, existing end-effector-centric methods neglect body-arm coordination, forcing the floating base to handle both coarse-scale displacements and fine-grained interactions, which compromises flight stability and restricts the operational workspace. To address these challenges, we propose CAMFlow, a unified framework that integrates latency-efficient generative learning with whole-body coordination control for aerial manipulation. First, we reformulate the generative process via Consistency Flow Matching, which compresses iterative denoising into efficient two-step trajectory generation for real-time control. Second, we introduce a coordination-aware action space, augmenting the end-effector pose with a relative body-arm state to explicitly model base-manipulator coupling. Third, we design a hierarchical whole-body Model Predictive Control scheme that grounds these high-level intents into dynamically feasible commands, ensuring end-effector tracking precision while maintaining the coordinated body-arm configuration. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CAMFlow achieves an inference latency of 37 ms, yielding a 3x speedup over diffusion baselines. By integrating real-time execution with active coordination, CAMFlow yields the highest success rates across benchmarks and significantly mitigates trajectory oscillations, enabling smooth and robust deployment in constrained and precision-demanding aerial manipulation tasks.

title: RoboBRIDGE: A Modular Framework for Bridging Policies to Robust Real-World Robotic Agents
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have attracted growing interest as a scalable approach to robotic manipulation. While these models are effective action predictors, deploying them as robotic agents exposes critical gaps: no mechanism for failure recovery, inconsistent execution over long horizons, and limited robustness to shifts in observations, tasks, or embodiments. Existing solutions address these limitations individually through model retraining or environment-specific modules, yet what is needed is a general framework that systematically transforms a pretrained VLA into a robotic agent. We present RoboBRIDGE, a modular framework that provides an orchestration layer over five coordinated modules, namely Monitor, Perceptor, Planner, Controller, and Robot Interface, to compose robust robotic agents from off-the-shelf components, including pretrained VLAs. The Monitor pairs rapid failure detection with hierarchical recovery to correct errors before they cascade. When the environment diverges from the current plan, the Planner triggers replanning while the Perceptor updates scene understanding asynchronously, avoiding execution stalls. Within the Controller, primitive skill fine-tuning factors manipulation into domain-invariant primitives with dedicated LoRA adapters, reducing sensitivity to domain shifts when a VLA is used. Across LIBERO, RoboCasa, and real-world case studies spanning multiple robot platforms and VLA backbones, RoboBRIDGE consistently outperforms both standalone policies and prior augmented VLA deployments. These results suggest that reliable robotic agency does not arise from scaling action predictors alone, but from structured orchestration around them.

title: MAG-PG: Mathematical Modeling Guided Multi-Agent LLM for Push–Grasping Synergy in Cluttered Scenes
abstract: Robust grasping in cluttered and occluded environments remains a persistent challenge in robotic manipulation, especially when the target object is blocked by surrounding obstacles. Traditional push-grasping strategies often rely on multi-step scene clearing and passive actions, which exhibit poor generalization and lack semantic understanding. To address this, we propose a push-grasping framework without task-specific policy training, enabling purposeful manipulation while avoiding redundant exploration. The system begins with a vision-language model that disentangles stacked scenes, converting 3D occlusions into 2D-accessible layouts. It then extracts spatial keypoints and obstacle abstractions, which are provided as inputs to a large language model to infer manipulation strategies with geometric awareness. A multi-agent architecture further handles task modeling, code generation, and logic validation without additional task-specific training. Extensive experiments in both simulated and real-world environments show that the system achieves higher grasp success rates and improved transferability across tested scenarios, demonstrating its effectiveness for cluttered tabletop manipulation.

title: RoboRetriever: Single-Camera Robot Object Retrieval Via Active and Interactive Perception with Dynamic Scene Graph
abstract: Humans effortlessly retrieve objects in cluttered, partially observable environments by combining visual reasoning, active viewpoint adjustment, and physical interaction—with only a single pair of eyes. In contrast, most existing robotic systems rely on carefully positioned fixed or multi-camera setups with complete scene visibility, which limits adaptability and incurs high hardware costs. We present RoboRetriever, a novel framework for real-world object retrieval that operates using only a single wrist-mounted RGB-D camera and free-form natural language instructions. RoboRetriever grounds visual observations to build and update a dynamic hierarchical scene graph that encodes object semantics, geometry, and inter-object relations over time. The supervisor module reasons over this memory and task instruction to infer the target object and coordinate an integrated action module combining active perception, and interactive perception. To enable task-aware scene-grounded active perception, we introduce a novel visual prompting scheme that leverages large reasoning vision-language models to determine 6-DoF camera poses aligned with the semantic task goal and geometry scene context. We evaluate RoboRetriever on diverse real-world object retrieval tasks, including scenarios with human intervention, demonstrating strong adaptability and robustness in cluttered scenes with only one RGB-D camera.

title: Agentic Scene Policies: Unifying Space, Semantics, and Affordances for Robot Action
abstract: Designing or learning robot policies that generalize zero-shot across a range of language instructions and objects is a core problem in robotics. Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) learn such policies end-to-end by repurposing existing Vision-Language Models (VLMs), but generalization to new instructions and objects remains challenging. An alternative is to implement a modular policy by leveraging an explicit VLM-based 3D scene representation and motion planning. While modular policies show strong zero-shot potential, they typically retrieve objects based on semantics without explicit spatial reasoning, severely restricting their overall grounding capabilities. They also interact with objects using basic grasping and navigation skills. In this work, we address these limitations by unifying grounding capabilities and robot skills in a single agentic action space through a scene-agent tool interface. By leveraging part-level affordances, our skills generalize across diverse objects and enable zero-shot interactions such as unplugging chargers and opening drawers. We name the resulting framework Agentic Scene Policies (ASP). Through extensive real-world experiments, we show how ASP consistently outperforms leading VLAs in the zero-shot setting. We also demonstrate the extensibility of our framework by introducing a mobile version of ASP to tackle room-level queries.

title: E³VT: An Effective and Efficient VLA Framework for Embodied Visual Tracking in the Wild
abstract: While end-to-end Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated remarkable success in structured tabletop manipulation, their deployment for Embodied Visual Tracking (EVT), which serves as a fundamental capability for mobile robot autonomy "in the wild," has received comparatively limited attention. Inherently characterized by continuous ego-motion and dynamic occlusions, EVT poses a complex Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP). This POMDP nature severely impedes the effective transfer of pretrained manipulation VLA models, as resolving partial observability necessitates integrating multi-frame, long-temporal visual contexts. Concurrently, processing these extended contexts poses a significant challenge to the efficiency and low-latency inference required for agile control. To overcome the resulting effectiveness-efficiency dilemma, we propose a novel VLA framework for EVT. Our approach, termed E³VT, resolves this dilemma through three targeted innovations. We introduce an inference-free spatial enhancement mechanism for robust target grounding, coupled with a history consistency constraint that natively embeds long-term temporal dependencies into trajectory generation. Furthermore, we employ a feature compression strategy to drastically reduce the computational load of processing these extended temporal visual contexts. Extensive simulations and real-world deployments demonstrate that our framework achieves state-of-the-art tracking robustness and sim-to-real generalization while sustaining the high inference frequencies demanded by agile mobile robots.

title: Long-Term Memory for VLA-Based Agents in Open-World Task Execution
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated significant potential for embodied decision-making; however, their application in complex chemical laboratory automation remains restricted by limited long-horizon reasoning and the absence of persistent experience accumulation. Existing frameworks typically treat planning and execution as decoupled processes, often failing to consolidate successful strategies, which results in inefficient trial-and-error in multi-stage protocols. In this paper, we propose ChemBot, a dual-layer, closed-loop framework that integrates an autonomous AI agent with a progress-aware VLA model Skill-VLA for hierarchical task decomposition and execution. ChemBot utilizes a dual-layer memory architecture to consolidate successful trajectories into retrievable assets, while a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server facilitates efficient sub-agent and tool orchestration. To address the inherent limitations of VLA models, we further implement a future-state-based asynchronous inference mechanism to mitigate trajectory discontinuities. Extensive experiments on collaborative robots demonstrate that ChemBot achieves superior operational safety, precision, and task success rates compared to existing VLA baselines in complex, long-horizon chemical experimentation.

title: BiliVLA: Scene-Aware Vision-Language-Action Model with Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Biliary Endoscopic Navigation
abstract: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is a technically demanding and safety-critical procedure, where cannulation-grade navigation is hindered by partial observability, pronounced stage structure, and substantial visual domain shift (e.g., fluids, specular highlights, and occlusions). We propose BiliVLA, a scene-aware Vision–Language–Action framework for autonomous biliary endoscopic navigation that jointly performs semantic target understanding, visual grounding, and discrete continuum actuation within a single instruction-conditioned policy. BiliVLA introduces (i) scene-aware supervision to promote target-consistent grounding under stage-specific language objectives and (ii) safety-aware supervision that triggers conservative recovery behavior upon luminal wall contact. We further adopt a two-stage training strategy that combines grounding-enhanced supervised fine-tuning with GRPO-based reward-guided policy optimization, improving localization fidelity and action reliability.To facilitate learning in this setting, we curate BiliVLA-Motion, a vision–language–kinematic dataset with 10k annotated image–motion pairs spanning Entry Navigation, Lumen Traversal, and Calculus Localization. Across held-out evaluation and real-world phantom deployments, BiliVLA achieves a mean mIoU of 0.9625 and an average action precision of 91.96%, with physical success rates of 72.73%, 100%, and 81.82%, respectively. Ablation studies confirm that both GRPO and scene-aware modeling are critical to robust execution. These results suggest that semantic grounding coupled with reward-driven refinement enables reliable closed-loop endoscopic navigation under challenging visual conditions.

title: ExtraGS: Enhancing Endoscopic View Extrapolation via Diffusion-Guided 3D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery (MIS) critically depends on reliable endoscopic perception for naviga_x0002_tion and safety. However, conventional endoscopes provide only a limited field of view, leaving large portions of surrounding anatomy unobserved. Recent neural rendering approaches, such as Neural Radiance Fields and 3D Gaussian Splatting, enable novel view synthesis from endoscopic videos, but their reliance on sparse observations often leads to severe artifacts when extrapolating beyond the training trajectory. In this work, we propose ExtraGS, a framework for enhancing endoscopic view extrapolation via diffusion-guided 3D Gaussian Splatting. Starting from an initial reconstruction, we introduce an uncertainty-guided virtual camera sampling strategy to actively explore blind spots and maximize information gain. The rendered views from these sampled locations are refined using a diffusion model to recover plausible anatomical structures, producing pseudo observations that guide further optimization. To prevent the generated content from degrading reliable regions, we adopt a confidence-weighted fine-tuning strategy when incorporating these pseudo observations. Extensive experiments on multiple public endoscopic datasets demonstrate that ExtraGS significantly reduces extrapolation artifacts and achieves state-of-the-art performance in endoscopic novel view synthesis. Code is available at https://github.com/IRMVLab/ExtraGS.

title: From Gaze to Action: A Hands-Free Robotic Ultrasound System Via Gaze-Embodied Perception
abstract: Large foundation models have popularized prompt based human machine interaction. In embodied intelligence, gaze naturally serves as a prompt to convey user intent in real time without verbal commands. Inspired by this, we presented a hands-free robotic ultrasound system (RUSS) and introduced a generalized learning paradigm for autonomous ultrasound imaging—GEPIC (Gaze-Empowered Perception and Interactive Control). GEPIC integrates data-driven policy learning and classical control, comprising four modules: gaze-empowered prompting, enhanced visual perception via foundation model finetuning, policy learning from demonstration, and visual servoing with compliance control. Through this framework, the robot autonomously performs perception, localization, stable contact, dynamic tracking, and complete ultrasound imaging of target organs under gaze guidance. Systematic evaluations on phantoms and human subjects demonstrate robust generalization across diverse anatomical structures and safe imaging performance. We envision that this gaze-embodied paradigm allows sonographers to perform concurrent clinical tasks, such as medical documentation or ultrasound-guided interventions, while the robot executes the scanning procedure. This work offers strong support for the next generation of collaborative medical robotics. The gaze-segmentation dataset developed in this study will be publicly released at https://github.com/RUSS464/MGaze-US.
